Damage-Mechanism Mapping per API RP 571 — ADNOC Service Specifics

ADNOC service-specific damage mechanisms: sulfidation §4.4.2 (Ruwais hydrocracker + crude trains, parabolic rate curves on carbon steel above 230°C); HTHA §5.1.3.1 (hydroprocessing units, Nelson curves per API RP 941); naphthenic-acid corrosion §4.4.7 (heavy-crude trains); amine cracking §5.1.2.3 (Habshan + Buhasa gas-treatment trains, NACE SP0472 PWHT triggers); sour-water cracking §5.1.2.4 + NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 hardness limits on sour-service piping; chloride SCC §4.5.1 (austenitic stainless seawater cooling on offshore + LNG cryogenic service); CUI §4.3.5 (Ruwais + Das Island coastal salt-laden air, per ADNOC GMTS-100 §12 strategy); MIC §5.1.1.6 (stagnant seawater cooling); HIC/SOHIC §5.1.2.4 (sour-service vessels per NACE MR0175); FAC §4.2.14 (Borouge utility steam). Atlantis runs damage-mechanism baselines as the foundation for RBI prioritisation and FFS triggering — see RBI program design and API 579 FFS.

Robotic + Drone Inspection — GMTS-100 §11 Allowance and Atlantis Field Stack

ADNOC GMTS-100 §11 explicitly allows drone-based VT on flare stacks + tank roofs + elevated structures, and robotic crawler MFL on tank bottoms + carbon-steel pipe. Atlantis Abu Dhabi field stack includes DJI Matrice 350 RTK with Zenmuse L2 LiDAR + P1 photogrammetry for drone-based VT + thermography; Silverwing Floormap + Eddyfi Sharck robotic MFL for tank bottoms; magnetic-wheeled UT crawlers for pipe; ROV-based subsea UT for offshore tie-ins. Robotic + drone inspection cuts scaffolding cost dramatically + reduces rope-access risk. Reporting integrates directly into Atlantis Digital Twin geometry overlay.
